item.title: Testing the Future of Joint All-Domain Operations in Africa
item.description: Africa’s open terrain could become the proving ground for next-generation warfare, helping the U.S. and partners test drones, electronic warfare, and joint all-domain operations while signaling deterrence to China and Russia.

item.title: The Many Faces of Antisemitic Terrorism in the United States
item.description: Anti-Jewish violence in America is no longer driven by one ideology alone. Neo-Nazis, jihadists, anti-Israel extremists, and even state-backed actors are converging on the same targets, stretching counterterrorism defenses and redefining domestic security threats.

item.title: Security and the Pacific Islands: Insights from Young Pacific Leaders
item.description: As strategic competition intensifies across the Pacific, emerging regional voices are redefining what security, partnership, and resilience should look like in the decades ahead.

item.title: Elevating Pacific Perspectives in U.S. Regional Security Cooperation
item.description: As Washington deepens its Pacific engagement, regional leaders are making clear that security means far more than defense alone.

item.title: How Arab Gulf States View the Emerging Iran Deal
item.description: A prospective deal between the United States and Iran could shape the contours of an emerging order in the Middle East. Gulf states are paying attention.

item.title: The Politics and Repercussions of Washington’s Permanent Joint Board on Defense Pause
item.description: The PJBD has long served as the quiet architecture of Canada-U.S. defense cooperation; its suspension risks weakening one of the few remaining forums for strategic trust and candid dialogue.

item.title: Economic Warfare and Military Power
item.description: As strategic competition intensifies, the United States needs a clearer way to use finance, trade, industrial policy, and regulation to strengthen its own defense base while making it harder for adversaries to turn economic strength into military power.

item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers May 27, 2026.

item.title: Rebuilding U.S. Missile Inventory: A Multiyear Project
item.description: High expenditure of key munitions in Operation Epic Fury has created a window of vulnerability until inventories return to pre-war levels and then reach levels that war planners desire.

item.title: NASA Changes Course on Commercial Space Stations
item.description: NASA is shifting (again) it's plans to maintain a human presence in low Earth orbit, making changes to how it will replace the International Space Station. These changes will add costs and delays. They are also a departure from NASA efforts to use as-a-service models to lay the foundations of a future space economy.

item.title: The Terrorist Threat to the 2026 World Cup
item.description: The 2026 World Cup will be the largest sporting event ever held and a magnet for terrorists of all stripes. A new CSIS brief examines who might attack, what targets are at greatest risk, and the countermeasures being deployed.

item.title: U.S.-India Insight: Mandate to Momentum: A Three Point Agenda for Indian States
item.description: Winning an election is the easy part. For India's newest state governments, the harder work starts now.

item.title: The Return of the Alien Tort Statute
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch outlines how the Alien Tort Statute is reemerging as a major legal issue, with a pending Supreme Court case potentially providing guidance to plaintiffs and companies on what torts are covered and who can be considered a defendant.

item.title: Latest U.S.-China Agriculture Talks Expand Purchasing Pledges Beyond Soybeans
item.description: The Trump-Xi Summit concluded with an agricultural purchase pledge thatwould return U.S.-China agricultural trade to pre-2025 levels if fulfilled.

item.title: What Is Maven Smart System, and What Does It Do?
item.description: Matt Mande and Gregory C. Allen provide a detailed overview Maven Smart System, the AI-powered software platform that has enabled a revolution in military targeting.

item.title: Why the West Keeps Losing Critical Mineral Assets to China
item.description: China is winning the race for critical minerals long before mines enter production. As Chinese firms acquire strategic mineral assets worldwide, the United States and its allies need new tools to identify, protect, and compete for ownership of future supply.

item.description: The CSIS Commission on U.S. Cyber Force Generation examines how the United States can build, organize, and sustain a dedicated cyber service.

item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch discusses the USMCA negotiations and ongoing Section 103 and Section 122 trade investigations.

item.title: The Next Caribbean Crisis? Assessing U.S. Military Options Toward Cuba
item.description: The United States has stepped up economic, political, and military pressure on Cuba. This commentary examines five possible scenarios involving the use of force against Cuba.
